topic_summary: Analysis of the Hagia Sophia's contested status between secular museum (1934-2020) and active mosque (2020-present). The 1934 conversion to museum under Atatürk framed the site as universal cultural heritage; the 2020 reconversion to mosque under Erdoğan reasserted Islamic sovereignty and worship primacy. The substrate—the physical monument with its layered Byzantine-Ottoman history—persists, but readings differ on what authority legitimately controls it and for whose benefit.

key_entities: Hagia Sophia (6th century Byzantine cathedral → Ottoman mosque 1453 → secular museum 1934 → mosque 2020)
Turkish State (sovereign authority over the site)
Atatürk / Turkish Republic founding ideology (secularist modernization)
Eastern Orthodox diaspora (historical claimants to Byzantine legacy)
key_tensions: Secularist universalism vs Islamic sovereignty (framing of legitimate site control)
National patrimony vs global heritage (Turkish state vs UNESCO jurisdiction claims)
Historical layering vs conquest priority (Byzantine foundation vs Ottoman conquest as legitimating event)

readings.commitment: The site's legitimacy derives from its status as shared human cultural heritage transcending any single religious or national claim
readings.authority_grounding: Atatürk's secularist state-building project plus UNESCO World Heritage regime; authority grounded in modernist universalism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Beneficiaries: global tourism/scholarship sector, secularist Turkish elites. Victim set: Islamic worship claims suppressed. Authority: technocratic museum administration under secular constitutional framework. High ε (tourism revenue, ideological signal of secular modernity).

readings.commitment: The site's legitimacy derives from the 1453 Ottoman conquest and continuous Islamic endowment (waqf), making it sovereign Islamic worship space under Turkish state authority
readings.authority_grounding: Conquest rights plus Turkish state sovereignty; authority grounded in post-Ottoman nation-state's right to define its own cultural patrimony and religious practice
readings.expected_structural_delta: Beneficiaries: AKP political coalition, Turkish Islamic constituency, broader Sunni ummah symbolically. Victim set: non-Muslim visitors (access restrictions), UNESCO regime (jurisdiction denied), secularist Turks (ideological defeat). Authority: executive decree validated by court reversal of 1934 ruling. Moderate-high ε (political consolidation, religious identity signal, diplomatic friction cost).

readings.commitment: The site's legitimacy derives from its founding as a Christian cathedral and should return to Orthodox ecclesiastical control or remain neutral to honor its Byzantine origins
readings.authority_grounding: Historical precedent of pre-conquest Christian status; authority grounded in civilizational continuity argument and restitution norms (though no viable enforcement mechanism exists)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Beneficiaries: Eastern Orthodox diaspora (symbolic), Greek state (diplomatic leverage). Victim set: Turkish sovereignty (external claim on national territory), Islamic worship continuity (interrupted again). Authority: external normative claim with no enforcement; practically dormant but ideologically active in Greek-Turkish tensions. Low ε in material terms (no realistic implementation pathway) but symbolically generative.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Universal heritage reading requires the site transcend sectarian ownership claims (neutrality axiom); Islamic sovereignty reading requires the site function as active worship space under religious authority (sectarian primacy axiom). No framework can simultaneously hold both as true: a neutral museum cannot be a functioning mosque, and a functioning mosque cannot maintain neutrality toward competing religious claims.

Islamic sovereignty reading grounds legitimacy in conquest and continuous Islamic endowment (conquest-as-title axiom); Orthodox restitution reading grounds legitimacy in pre-conquest Christian foundation and denies conquest as legitimate title transfer (conquest-as-illegitimate axiom). These axioms are mutually exclusive: accepting conquest as legitimate title requires rejecting restitution claims, and vice versa.

omegas.description: Universal_heritage and islamic_sovereignty readings both remain socially live despite axiom contradiction—this is licensed plurality. The coexists_with edge type documents this: contradictory axioms, stable coexistence, no synthesis pathway. Orthodox_restitution has foreclosed edge (dormant in enforcement terms).

Does the Ottoman waqf endowment have continuous legal force, or was it legally extinguished by the 1934 decree? If extinguished, the 2020 reconversion is new policy (Piton) rather than restoration of standing law (Rope). Turkish jurisprudence treats waqf as never extinguished, but this remains contested.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)—legal continuity assumption unexamined in readings
